items.body:
The v2 migration guide (`MIGRATION.md`, "Router" section) links rou3 to `https://rou3.h3.dev/`. That host has no DNS record, so the link fails. This points it at the rou3 repository, https://github.com/h3js/rou3.

Docs only.

items.title: fix(response): merge `Vary` headers instead of overwriting
items.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

Closes #1642.

### ❓ Type of change

- [ ] 📖 Documentation (updates to the documentation, readme, or JSdoc annotations)
- [x] 🐞 Bug fix (a non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] 👌 Enhancement (improving an existing functionality like performance)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (a non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🧹 Chore (updates to the build process or auxiliary tools and libraries)
- [ ] ⚠️ Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)

### 📚 Description

Previously, `mergeHeaders` in `src/response.ts` used `target.set(name, value)` for every header except `set-cookie`. When middleware staged a `Vary` header (e.g. `Accept-Encoding` or `Origin`) on `event.res.headers` or `event.res.errHeaders`, it would overwrite the `Vary` header of a returned `Response` / `HTTPResponse` / `HTTPError`.

This PR updates `mergeHeaders` to merge `Vary` values:
- Deduplicates header names case-insensitively while preserving the first occurrence's casing.
- Collapses to `*` when either side includes `*` (per RFC 9110 §12.5.5).
- Applies uniformly to `Response`, `HTTPResponse`, and `HTTPError` (`errHeaders`) via `mergeHeaders`.

### 🧪 Verification

- `pnpm lint` (`oxlint` + `oxfmt`): 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `pnpm typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`): 0 errors.
- Added unit tests in `test/app.test.ts` covering `Vary` merging, case-insensitive deduplication, `*` collapsing, and `errHeaders` merging.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * `Vary` header values are now combined when response headers are merged, rather than replacing existing values. Entries are trimmed, duplicate values are removed without changing their original spelling or order, and `*` is preserved if it appears in either value. This applies to prepared response headers and error response headers; other headers retain their existing merge behavior.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
